1. The Mothership DaemonThe system orchestrator. It does not sit in the active control loop. Instead, it boots first, requests hugepages from the Linux kernel, initializes the shared memory canvas, validates hardware device permissions, pins subsequent worker threads to isolated CPU cores, and maintains passive telemetry logs. If any node fails or panics, Mothership coordinates controlled degradation or graceful restart procedures without allowing actuators to enter high-impedance drift.2. The Explorer NodeThe exploratory engine. Typically implemented in Python or C++ with high-level framework bindings (such as LibTorch or TensorRT). It ingests high-latency sensory data (cameras, depth sensors, environmental context) and continuously explores policy parameter space, computes global plans, or refines behavioral weights. It publishes candidate decisions or updated neural weights into shared memory at whatever cadence it can manage, entirely unconstrained by hard clock ticks.3. The Fast Decision NodeThe mid-level tactical driver. Implemented in modern deterministic C++, it runs synchronously at a fixed rate (e.g., 200 Hz to 1 kHz). It combines local state estimates with the most recent validated policy or trajectory produced by the Explorer Node. It synthesizes unconstrained joint commands, task-space wrenches, or nominal path vectors. Because it does not guarantee absolute physical safety against dynamic changes or unmodeled obstacles, its output is treated strictly as an intent, not an execution mandate.4. The Guardrail NodeThe safety gatekeeper. Built in memory-safe systems languages (typically Rust), it consumes the unconstrained intent from the Fast Decision Node and the current verified state of the robot. It maintains mathematical models of all known physical boundaries: joint limits, velocity ceilings, thermal limits, self-collision envelopes, and dynamic obstacle perimeters. Using optimization methods like Quadratic Programming, it computes the minimal intervention needed to alter the requested command such that the robot remains safely within its admissible operational envelope.5. The MiddleMan (HAL Bridge)The physical interface. Running with root/real-time privileges, it converts safe command envelopes into low-level electrical drive protocols (EtherCAT CST frames, CANopen packets, or PWM duty cycles). It also reads raw encoder registers, IMUs, and current sensors, populating the primary telemetry buffers for all upstream consumers. Crucially, it houses an independent, hardware-level watchdog loop that cuts bus power or engages mechanical brakes if the software fails to refresh its command within a hard time budget.MODULE 24: SAFETY PHILOSOPHY, CBF PRACTICES & SIM-TO-REAL PARADIGMS24.1 WHY CONTROL BARRIER FUNCTIONS REPLACE TRADITIONAL CLIPPINGIn naive robotic software architectures, safety boundaries are implemented via heuristic clamping or rule-based state machines:If position exceeds threshold, set velocity to zero.If an obstacle is detected within 50 cm, command emergency stop.If torque exceeds limit, clip to maximum allowed value.These naive methods create dangerous side effects in multi-degree-of-freedom, high-inertia platforms:Kinetic Energy Traps: Clipping velocity or acceleration abruptly ignores system momentum. A heavy robotic arm moving at high speed toward a joint limit cannot stop instantaneously; clamping velocity when the boundary is breached will still lead to mechanical impact due to actuator saturation.Boundary Chattering & Limit Cycles: Abrupt rule switches introduce discontinuous vector fields, causing high-frequency oscillations (chatter) around safety thresholds. This induces mechanical fatigue, motor overheating, and sensor noise spikes.Deadlocks: Emergency stops freeze the system without providing a dynamically feasible recovery trajectory, requiring manual human resets in industrial environments.Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) solve these issues by evaluating safety forward in time. Instead of asking "am I safe right now?", a CBF evaluates "is there an admissible control input right now that guarantees I can remain safe in the future, given my current momentum and actuator capacity?"By transforming safety constraints into continuous, affine inequalities over the control inputs, the Guardrail Node acts as a smooth filter. When the robot operates well inside safe margins, the Guardrail passes the Fast Decision Node's intents with zero modification. As the system approaches a safety boundary, the Guardrail smoothly deflects the trajectory along the tangent of the barrier, preserving operational momentum while guaranteeing constraint satisfaction.24.2 THE SIM-TO-REAL GAP: CAUSES, MITIGATIONS, AND TESTINGDeploying machine learning models and dynamic controllers trained in virtual environments onto real-world hardware is notoriously difficult. In simulation, gravity is exact, time can be paused, friction is uniform, and sensor data arrives on schedule. In the physical world, physics engines are imperfect, sensors are noisy, and mechanical structures flex.Primary Causes of Sim-to-Real Discrepancy:Actuator Dynamics & Latency: Most physics engines simulate ideal motors that achieve commanded torques instantaneously. Real brushless DC motors suffer from phase inductance, current loop rise times, gear backlash, and rotor inertia.Friction and Contact Nonlinearities: Coulomb and viscous friction models in simulation fail to capture stick-slip transitions, temperature-dependent grease viscosity, and surface compliance.Structural Elasticity: Simulation platforms often assume perfectly rigid links. High-payload manipulators and quadruped legs experience noticeable structural deflection under high acceleration.Sensor Noise and Asynchrony: Real IMUs drift, optical encoders suffer from quantization and vibration noise, and vision feeds experience motion blur and variable exposure latencies.Engineering Strategies for Mitigating the Gap:Domain Randomization: During policy training in simulation, physical parameters (link masses, friction coefficients, center-of-mass locations, actuator delays, and sensory noise profiles) should be randomized across wide distributions at every rollout episode. This forces the policy to learn robust features rather than overfitting to specific simulation artifacts.Actuator Net Modeling: Train small, high-fidelity neural networks or system-identification models on physical motor dyno data to predict true torque output given recent command and velocity histories. Embed this actuator network directly into the simulation loop.Conservative Invariant Envelopes: When defining safety barriers in the Guardrail Node, deliberately shrink the admissible state boundary by an uncertainty margin proportional to the maximum identified modeling error. The high-level policy can explore aggressively inside this conservative bubble without risking physical harm.Iterative Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Progression:Phase 1 (Software-in-the-Loop): All nodes run on developer workstations against full physics engines (e.g., Isaac Sim, MuJoCo).Phase 2 (Hardware-in-the-Loop): Production embedded compute boxes (e.g., Jetson Orin, industrial PCs) execute the full compiled software stack, driving simulated actuators over real network interfaces.Phase 3 (Dynamometer Verification): Physical motors and gearboxes run unmounted on test benches, driven through extreme torque transients to validate thermal models and safety shutoffs.Phase 4 (Tethered Low-Power Bringup): The physical robot is suspended or tethered, running on current-limited power supplies with 10% safety limits, gradually scaling to 100% operational velocity.MODULE 25: REAL-TIME OPERATING SYSTEMS & PLATFORM INFRASTRUCTURESoftware determinism is impossible without continuous operating system support. Standard general-purpose operating systems optimize for average-case throughput rather than worst-case execution time, making them unsuitable for real-time robotic control out of the box.25.1 LINUX PREEMPT_RT ESSENTIALSThe standard Linux kernel prioritizes background batch processing, file system caching, and fair resource sharing. A thread can be arbitrarily preempted or delayed by kernel locks, interrupts, or page cache flushes. The PREEMPT_RT patch transforms Linux into a hard real-time operating system by altering fundamental kernel mechanics:Making Spinlocks Preemptible: In standard Linux, code executing inside a spinlock disables kernel preemption. Under PREEMPT_RT, spinlocks are converted into sleeping mutexes (rt_mutex), allowing high-priority real-time threads to preempt code running inside critical sections.Threaded Interrupt Handlers: Hardware interrupts (IRQs) are forced to run in dedicated kernel threads. This allows real-time user-space control tasks to be scheduled at a higher priority than hardware interrupt handlers, preventing network cards or USB ports from starving control loops.Priority Inheritance Mutexes: To prevent priority inversion—where a low-priority thread holding a shared lock blocks a high-priority thread while being preempted by an intermediate-priority task—rt_mutex automatically elevates the low-priority thread's priority to match the blocked thread until the lock is released.25.2 PROCESSOR AFFINITY, CORE ISOLATION, AND CACHE WARMINGTo achieve microsecond-level determinism on modern multi-core processors (such as AMD EPYC, Intel Xeon, or ARM Cortex-A78AE), control threads must be physically isolated from the rest of the OS:Kernel Core Isolation (isolcpus / nohz_full): By passing configuration parameters to the Linux bootloader, specific CPU cores (e.g., Cores 2 and 3) are completely removed from the general OS scheduler. The kernel will never assign arbitrary background tasks, user shell commands, or software timers to these cores.Interrupt Shielding (irqbalance exclusions): Ensure that hardware device interrupts (Ethernet, PCIe, NVMe) are routed exclusively to non-isolated housekeeping cores (such as Core 0 and Core 1).Thread Pinning: Real-time worker threads (GuardrailNode and MiddleMan) are explicitly pinned to isolated cores using processor affinity directives (pthread_setaffinity_np). Once pinned, they run uninterrupted from initialization to shutdown.Memory Locking (mlockall): A major source of latency spikes is page faulting—when a thread accesses a memory address that has been swapped to disk or has not yet been physically mapped by the memory management unit (MMU). Real-time processes must lock their entire virtual address space into physical RAM on startup, pre-faulting the stack and heap to ensure that memory accesses never trigger MMU page faults during runtime.Cache Line Warming: Before entering nominal control execution, real-time algorithms should cycle through their working data structures several times to ensure all critical instructions and lookup tables reside in L1/L2 instruction and data caches.MODULE 26: COMMON FAILURE PATTERNS & ROOT CAUSE ANALYSISUnderstanding how robotic software fails in practice is essential for building resilient systems. Below are three of the most pervasive failure modes encountered in complex autonomous architectures, along with practical diagnosis and remediation strategies.26.1 THE "FROZEN OBSERVER" (DIVERGENCE UNDER COGNITIVE OVERLOAD)Manifestation:The robot suddenly drifts or continues along an outdated trajectory despite an imminent physical obstacle. Diagnostic logs show that the state estimation filter or high-level planner is still publishing data, but the published state does not reflect physical reality.Root Cause:The high-level vision pipeline or local mapper encountered a complex scene with high geometric entropy (e.g., entering an environment with dense foliage, reflective surfaces, or crowds). The feature extractor or point-cloud registration algorithm exceeded its allocated frame budget. Rather than dropping stale frames, the node's internal queue buffered them.The filter fell progressively further behind physical reality, processing sensor data that was hundreds of milliseconds old. The downstream controller operated correctly relative to the reported state, but the reported state lagged real-world events.Remediation:Zero-Depth Queue Policies: High-rate state estimators must never buffer incoming perception data. Set sensory ingestion queues to a depth of 1, configured to overwrite old data on overflow.Heartbeat Latency Checks: Every state packet must carry a monotonic hardware timestamp indicating when the physical photon or encoder pulse was acquired. The Guardrail Node must immediately reject any control input computed from telemetry older than a fixed safety budget (e.g., >50 ms).26.2 SENSOR DROPOUTS AND STALE-STATE RESIDUALSManifestation:An autonomous system experiences brief, violent torque twitches across multiple joints, followed by an immediate emergency shutdown or protective trip.Root Cause:A physical sensor (e.g., a wheel encoder or CAN-based absolute bus encoder) experienced an intermittent hardware disconnect or electrical noise burst, dropping two or three consecutive measurement frames.The estimator was programmed to "hold last known good value" when data was missing. When the connection restored, the newly measured position differed significantly from the held value. The numerical differentiator interpreted this step change as an instantaneous velocity spike ($\Delta x / \Delta t \to \infty$), causing the derivative ($D$) term of the feedback controller to output maximum torque for a single cycle.Remediation:Never Use Step Interpolation for Numerical Differentiation: When sensor updates are missed, the state estimator must propagate state forward using system kinematics and model predictions, rather than holding raw values constant.Derivative Low-Pass Filtering & Sanity Limits: Apply first-order or second-order low-pass filters to all velocity and acceleration estimates derived from discrete positional measurements. Impose physically bounded acceleration limits beyond which single-frame derivative spikes are clamped.26.3 REINFORCEMENT LEARNING "POLICY LAZINESS"Manifestation:During deployment on physical hardware, an RL-driven locomotion or manipulation policy performs well initially, but gradually becomes unresponsive, sluggish, or settles into a static, rigid posture, refusing to track target objectives.Root Cause:The reward formulation over-penalized safety interventions or high-frequency torque usage relative to task completion rewards. Over thousands of training iterations, the policy discovered that attempting challenging maneuvers occasionally triggered safety barrier penalties from the Guardrail Node.To maximize its cumulative reward, the policy learned that remaining completely stationary or moving at near-zero velocity minimizes safety penalty risks, effectively discovering a degenerate local optimum: "do nothing, and you cannot violate safety."Remediation:Intervention Shaping: Instead of applying a massive negative reward spike when the Guardrail modifies an action, penalize only the $L_2$ norm of the deviation between the proposed action and the safe action $(\Vert u_{\text{proposed}} - u_{\text{safe}} \Vert^2)$. This provides a smooth gradient that guides the policy back toward the safe boundary rather than discouraging movement entirely.Curriculum-Based Constraint Injection: Train the initial policy in an unconstrained environment until task competence is established, then gradually introduce safety barrier boundaries and penalty weights as training progresses.MODULE 27: BRINGUP PROTOCOLS, TELEMETRY & POST-MORTEM ANALYSISDeploying a complex robotic software stack onto physical hardware demands disciplined, repeatable procedures. Skipping steps during hardware bringup frequently leads to damaged equipment, broken gearboxes, and safety risks.27.1 THE SYSTEMATIC HARDWARE BRINGUP CHECKLISTBefore any autonomous code is permitted to command current to actuators, the engineering team must complete a staged verification procedure:[Level 0: Physical & Electrical Integrity]
  ├── Verify bus supply voltages with an oscilloscope under simulated load.
  ├── Check E-Stop loop circuit continuity (hardware-wired, non-software dependent).
  └── Inspect absolute encoder alignments and mechanical hardstops.
          │ PASS
          v
[Level 1: Communication & Watchdog Timing]
  ├── Verify bus communication cycle jitter (< 10 us on EtherCAT / CAN).
  ├── Validate hardware watchdog trip: forcibly kill software and verify brakes engage in < 5 ms.
  └── Confirm zero packet loss over a continuous 1-hour idle stress test.
          │ PASS
          v
[Level 2: Directionality & Kinematics Validation]
  ├── Command low open-loop currents (5% rated) to each actuator individually.
  ├── Verify positive commanded torque produces positive encoder position delta.
  └── Confirm joint limits in software match physical mechanical stops.
          │ PASS
          v
[Level 3: Closed-Loop Gravity Compensation]
  ├── Enable model-based gravity compensation with zero reference tracking.
  ├── The robot should feel "weightless" when moved by hand (zero backdrive resistance).
  └── Ensure no joint drifts or experiences high-frequency vibration.
          │ PASS
          v
[Level 4: Full Autonomous Execution]
  ├── Enable Guardrail Node with conservative safety barrier margins.
  ├── Enable Fast Decision Node with trajectory scaling capped at 10% nominal velocity.
  └── Gradually scale velocity envelope to 100% while monitoring thermal and tracking margins.
27.2 CIRCULAR TELEMETRY BUFFERS & POST-MORTEM FLIGHT RECORDERSWhen a robot exhibits anomalous physical behavior or encounters an emergency shutdown, engineers need high-resolution data from the moments immediately preceding the event. However, streaming gigabytes of raw sensor and diagnostic data continuously over wireless links to off-board servers is impractical.The production approach involves implementing an on-board circular black-box flight recorder:Pre-allocated Ring Buffers in Memory: Allocate a fixed memory region (e.g., 512 MB of RAM) partitioned into circular buffers.High-Frequency Writes: Every iteration of the GuardrailNode and MiddleMan writes joint states, raw torques, filter residuals, QP solver iterations, and hardware bus statuses into this memory region at full control rates (1 kHz). No disk I/O occurs during nominal operation.Triggered Snapshot Flushing: If a safety barrier trips, an E-stop is triggered, or an anomalous innovation residual is detected, the flight recorder freezes the circular buffer and flushes a window (e.g., the 10 seconds preceding the event and 2 seconds following it) directly to non-volatile NVMe storage.Offline Post-Mortem Visualization: Engineers can inspect the captured snapshot frame-by-frame, evaluating the exact state of the QP solver, the raw sensor readings, and the operating system scheduler metrics at the microsecond the failure occurred.MODULE 28: DEVELOPER INTERACTION PLAYBOOKS & ARCHITECTURAL DECISION MATRIXWhen extending the Shiva.ai framework or adapting it to new hardware platforms, engineers regularly face high-level architectural decisions. Below is a structured guide to resolving common architectural dilemmas.28.1 ARCHITECTURAL DECISION MATRIXArchitectural DilemmaRecommended ApproachJustificationInter-Node Communication(ROS 2 DDS vs. POSIX Shared Memory)Use POSIX Shared Memory for all intra-machine control paths (MiddleMan, Guardrail, Decision). Reserve ROS 2 / DDS strictly for off-board telemetry and visualization.DDS serialization adds unpredictable latency (50–500 µs) and dynamic heap allocations, breaking hard real-time determinism.Safety Barrier Implementation(Heuristic Clamping vs. Optimization CBFs)Use Optimization-based CBFs (QP Projection).Heuristic clamping creates momentum traps, induces high-frequency chatter, and fails to handle coupled multi-joint dynamics.Language Selection(C++ vs. Rust for Guardrail)Use Rust for the Guardrail Node; use C++20 for performance-critical legacy math libraries.Rust guarantees memory safety, eliminates data races at compile time, and prevents undefined behavior in the critical safety layer.OS Scheduling Class(SCHED_OTHER vs. SCHED_FIFO)Use SCHED_FIFO (priority 80–95) on isolated cores for real-time nodes; use SCHED_OTHER for high-level perception and planning.SCHED_OTHER allows the OS to preempt control loops for arbitrary housekeeping tasks, introducing dangerous latency jitter.Queue Management(Deep Buffering vs. Overwrite on Arrival)Use Overwrite on Arrival (Depth = 1) for all real-time sensory and state-estimation channels.Buffered sensor data leads to the "frozen observer" failure mode, where controllers make decisions based on outdated physical reality.28.2 FIELD WORKFLOW: TUNING CONTROL BARRIER FUNCTION CONSERVATISMWhen commissioning a new physical platform, finding the right balance between safety and performance in the Guardrail Node is a common challenge. If safety margins are too conservative, the robot will be sluggish and fail to achieve its operational goals. If margins are too loose, the system risks mechanical collisions during dynamic transients.Recommended Field Tuning Protocol:Start with Physical Deceleration Limits: Determine the true maximum deceleration $a_{\text{max}}$ your actuators can provide without slipping belts, exceeding peak motor currents, or tipping the base. Never configure safety margins based on theoretical unmounted motor ratings.Establish the Class $\mathcal{K}$ Barrier Function: For a distance-to-boundary barrier $h(x) = d - d_{\text{min}}$, the CBF condition requires:$$\dot{h}(x) \ge -\gamma h(x)$$The parameter $\gamma > 0$ dictates how aggressively the controller is allowed to approach the boundary.Calibrate the Linear Gain $\gamma$:Begin with a very small value ($\gamma = 0.5$). The robot will decelerate well in advance of the obstacle, resembling a heavily damped cushion.Incrementally increase $\gamma$ while commanding aggressive step inputs toward a virtual boundary.Monitor the QP intervention metric: the difference between commanded torque and output torque.Stop increasing $\gamma$ when peak deceleration during safety intervention reaches 80% of the platform's verified physical deceleration limit $a_{\text{max}}$. The remaining 20% serves as a safety reserve for unexpected friction loss or payload variations.Validate Across Multi-Joint Dynamic Couplings: Verify that moving a distal joint (e.g., wrist or end-effector) at high speed does not cause an unexpected barrier intervention on a proximal joint (e.g., shoulder or waist) due to inertial coupling forces. If coupling causes false-positive safety trips, ensure the barrier formulation accounts for full multi-body inertia matrices rather than treating axes independently.

```rust
    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_pitch_topple_limit_2 | Invariant expr: 0.39 - abs(pitch_angle) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.39 - abs(pitch_angle)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.39 - abs(pitch_angle)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_pitch_topple_limit_2 });
        // CBF: cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_2 | Invariant expr: 4.5 - abs(v_linear) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("4.5 - abs(v_linear)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("4.5 - abs(v_linear)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_2 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

#### Rust Guardrail Implementation (Active-Set CBF QP Projection):
```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for fast_steering_mirror_piezo_laser_case_0010
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0010Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_10: f64,
    gamma_cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_10: f64,
    gamma_cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_10: f64,
}

impl FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0010Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_10: 55.30,
            gamma_cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_10: 44.00,
            gamma_cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_10: 31.40,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_10 | Invariant expr: 131.51 - piezo_voltage_x (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("131.51 - piezo_voltage_x");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("131.51 - piezo_voltage_x");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_10 });
        // CBF: cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_10 | Invariant expr: piezo_voltage_x - 0.0 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("piezo_voltage_x - 0.0");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("piezo_voltage_x - 0.0");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_10 });
        // CBF: cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_10 | Invariant expr: 23.08 - sqrt(jitter_quadrant_px^2 + jitter_quadrant_py^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("23.08 - sqrt(jitter_quadrant_px^2 + jitter_quadrant_py^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("23.08 - sqrt(jitter_quadrant_px^2 + jitter_quadrant_py^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_10 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

#### C++20 Fast Decision Node Real-Time Implementation:
```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for fast_steering_mirror_piezo_laser_case_0010
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>
#include <shiva/shared_memory_ring.hpp>
#include <array>
#include <chrono>

class FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0010FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0010FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(200) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 2> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_piezo_voltage_x(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_piezo_voltage_y(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

#### Python Policy / Explorer Integration (PyTorch / Shiva Bindings):
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from shiva_bindings import MiddleManClient

class FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0010Policy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, obs_dim=4, act_dim=2):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(obs_dim, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, act_dim)
        )
    def forward(self, state):
        return self.net(state)

policy = FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0010Policy()
# Real-time cyclic sync at 5000 Hz
```

```rust
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct Collaborative6DofArmCase0012Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,

    gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_12: f64,
    gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_12: f64,
}

impl Collaborative6DofArmCase0012Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(6),
            gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_12: 22.60,
            gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_12: 12.80,
            gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_12: 12.40,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_12 | Invariant expr: 19.57 - tau_ext_norm (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("19.57 - tau_ext_norm");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("19.57 - tau_ext_norm");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_12 });
        // CBF: cbf_self_collision_distance_12 | Invariant expr: dist_mesh - 0.04 (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("dist_mesh - 0.04");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("dist_mesh - 0.04");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_12 });
        // CBF: cbf_j2_pos_limit_12 | Invariant expr: 2.47 - abs(q2) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("2.47 - abs(q2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("2.47 - abs(q2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_12 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
```

```rust
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("z - 0.25");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_min_altitude_ground_14 });
        // CBF: cbf_max_tilt_angle_14 | Invariant expr: 0.85 - acos(cos(roll)*cos(pitch)) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.85 - acos(cos(roll)*cos(pitch))");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.85 - acos(cos(roll)*cos(pitch))");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_max_tilt_angle_14 });
        // CBF: cbf_ceiling_boundary_14 | Invariant expr: 24.17 - z (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("24.17 - z");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("24.17 - z");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_ceiling_boundary_14 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
```

```rust
impl CubesatReactionWheelCase0015Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(3),
            gamma_cbf_rw_speed_saturation_15: 8.60,
            gamma_cbf_payload_sun_exclusion_15: 13.40,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for chemical_cstr_temperature_ph_case_0017
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct ChemicalCstrTemperaturePhCase0017Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_thermal_runaway_trip_17: f64,
    gamma_cbf_reactor_underpressure_17: f64,
}

impl ChemicalCstrTemperaturePhCase0017Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_thermal_runaway_trip_17: 8.90,
            gamma_cbf_reactor_underpressure_17: 11.10,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_thermal_runaway_trip_17 | Invariant expr: 378.78 - reactor_temp_k (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("378.78 - reactor_temp_k");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("378.78 - reactor_temp_k");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_thermal_runaway_trip_17 });
        // CBF: cbf_reactor_underpressure_17 | Invariant expr: reactor_pressure_bar - 1.1 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("reactor_pressure_bar - 1.1");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("reactor_pressure_bar - 1.1");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_reactor_underpressure_17 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(10000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 2> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_coolant_valve_flow(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_feed_flow_rate(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```rust
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0020Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_20: f64,
    gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_20: f64,
    gamma_cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_20: f64,
    gamma_cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_20: f64,
    gamma_cbf_inverter_overcurrent_magnitude_20: f64,
}

impl BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0020Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_20: 24.40,
            gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_20: 28.30,
            gamma_cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_20: 15.80,
            gamma_cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_20: 16.80,
            gamma_cbf_inverter_overcurrent_magnitude_20: 36.20,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_20 | Invariant expr: 53.59 - grid_freq_hz (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("53.59 - grid_freq_hz");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("53.59 - grid_freq_hz");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_20 });
        // CBF: cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_20 | Invariant expr: grid_freq_hz - 53.58 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("grid_freq_hz - 53.58");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("grid_freq_hz - 53.58");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_20 });
        // CBF: cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_20 | Invariant expr: 93.61 - bess_soc_pct (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("93.61 - bess_soc_pct");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("93.61 - bess_soc_pct");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_20 });
        // CBF: cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_20 | Invariant expr: bess_soc_pct - 9.77 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("bess_soc_pct - 9.77");
```

```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for bess_grid_forming_inverter_frequency_case_0020
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>
#include <shiva/shared_memory_ring.hpp>
#include <array>
#include <chrono>

class BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0020FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0020FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(5000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 2> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_target_active_power_kw(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_target_reactive_power_kvar(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from shiva_bindings import MiddleManClient

class BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0020Policy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, obs_dim=6, act_dim=2):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(obs_dim, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, act_dim)
```

```cpp
class DoublePendulumCase0022FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit DoublePendulumCase0022FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(1000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 2> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_tau1(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_tau2(telemetry);

    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```rust
pub struct WheeledInvertedPendulumSegwayCase0024Guardrail {

    gamma_cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_24: f64,

impl WheeledInvertedPendulumSegwayCase0024Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_pitch_topple_limit_24: 15.80,
            gamma_cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_24: 6.90,
        }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {

        // CBF: cbf_pitch_topple_limit_24 | Invariant expr: 0.43 - abs(pitch_angle) (Degree 2)
```

```rust
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(3),
```

#### Rust Guardrail Implementation (Active-Set CBF QP Projection):
```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for fast_steering_mirror_piezo_laser_case_0032
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0032Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_32: f64,
    gamma_cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_32: f64,
    gamma_cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_32: f64,
}

impl FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0032Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_32: 47.60,
            gamma_cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_32: 55.70,
            gamma_cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_32: 31.80,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_32 | Invariant expr: 134.24 - piezo_voltage_x (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("134.24 - piezo_voltage_x");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("134.24 - piezo_voltage_x");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_piezo_max_voltage_depolarization_32 });
        // CBF: cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_32 | Invariant expr: piezo_voltage_x - 0.0 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("piezo_voltage_x - 0.0");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("piezo_voltage_x - 0.0");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_piezo_shear_depolarization_32 });
        // CBF: cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_32 | Invariant expr: 22.98 - sqrt(jitter_quadrant_px^2 + jitter_quadrant_py^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("22.98 - sqrt(jitter_quadrant_px^2 + jitter_quadrant_py^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("22.98 - sqrt(jitter_quadrant_px^2 + jitter_quadrant_py^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_psd_optical_aperture_bound_32 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

#### C++20 Fast Decision Node Real-Time Implementation:
```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for fast_steering_mirror_piezo_laser_case_0032
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>
#include <shiva/shared_memory_ring.hpp>
#include <array>
#include <chrono>

class FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0032FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0032FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(200) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 2> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_piezo_voltage_x(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_piezo_voltage_y(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

#### Python Policy / Explorer Integration (PyTorch / Shiva Bindings):
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from shiva_bindings import MiddleManClient

class FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0032Policy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, obs_dim=4, act_dim=2):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(obs_dim, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, act_dim)
        )
    def forward(self, state):
        return self.net(state)

# Hardware Deployment Initialization
client = MiddleManClient(bus_interface="MiddleMan_EtherCAT_CST")
policy = FastSteeringMirrorPiezoLaserCase0032Policy()
# Real-time cyclic sync at 5000 Hz
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for collaborative_6dof_arm_case_0034
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct Collaborative6DofArmCase0034Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_34: f64,
    gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_34: f64,
    gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_34: f64,
}

impl Collaborative6DofArmCase0034Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(6),
            gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_34: 19.80,
            gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_34: 14.70,
            gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_34: 10.90,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_34 | Invariant expr: 23.73 - tau_ext_norm (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("23.73 - tau_ext_norm");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("23.73 - tau_ext_norm");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_34 });
        // CBF: cbf_self_collision_distance_34 | Invariant expr: dist_mesh - 0.04 (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("dist_mesh - 0.04");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("dist_mesh - 0.04");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_34 });
        // CBF: cbf_j2_pos_limit_34 | Invariant expr: 2.33 - abs(q2) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("2.33 - abs(q2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("2.33 - abs(q2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_34 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 6> u_nominal;

        u_nominal[5] = compute_policy_tau6(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
```

#### Rust Guardrail Implementation (Active-Set CBF QP Projection):
```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for spacecraft_rcs_docking_case_0037
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0037Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_approach_corridor_cone_37: f64,
    gamma_cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_37: f64,
}

impl SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0037Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(3),
            gamma_cbf_approach_corridor_cone_37: 12.50,
            gamma_cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_37: 9.00,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_approach_corridor_cone_37 | Invariant expr: rel_x * tan(0.26) - sqrt(rel_y^2 + rel_z^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("rel_x * tan(0.26) - sqrt(rel_y^2 + rel_z^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("rel_x * tan(0.26) - sqrt(rel_y^2 + rel_z^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_approach_corridor_cone_37 });
        // CBF: cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_37 | Invariant expr: 0.26 - abs(rel_vx) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.26 - abs(rel_vx)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.26 - abs(rel_vx)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_37 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

#### C++20 Fast Decision Node Real-Time Implementation:
```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for spacecraft_rcs_docking_case_0037
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>
#include <shiva/shared_memory_ring.hpp>
#include <array>
#include <chrono>

class SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0037FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0037FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(10000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 3> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_thruster_fx(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_thruster_fy(telemetry);
        u_nominal[2] = compute_policy_thruster_fz(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```rust
pub struct FlywheelKineticUpsFrequencyCase0042Guardrail {

    gamma_cbf_min_extraction_speed_42: f64,

impl FlywheelKineticUpsFrequencyCase0042Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(1),
            gamma_cbf_burst_overspeed_centrifugal_42: 34.30,
            gamma_cbf_magnetic_touchdown_bearing_gap_42: 41.30,
            gamma_cbf_min_extraction_speed_42: 23.00,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_burst_overspeed_centrifugal_42 | Invariant expr: 54568.5 - rotor_speed_rpm (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("54568.5 - rotor_speed_rpm");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("54568.5 - rotor_speed_rpm");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_burst_overspeed_centrifugal_42 });
        // CBF: cbf_magnetic_touchdown_bearing_gap_42 | Invariant expr: 66.07 - rotor_radial_runout_um (Degree 1)

        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("66.07 - rotor_radial_runout_um");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_magnetic_touchdown_bearing_gap_42 });
        // CBF: cbf_min_extraction_speed_42 | Invariant expr: rotor_speed_rpm - 15000.0 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("rotor_speed_rpm - 15000.0");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("rotor_speed_rpm - 15000.0");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_min_extraction_speed_42 });
```

#### Rust Guardrail Implementation (Active-Set CBF QP Projection):
```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for collaborative_6dof_arm_case_0045
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct Collaborative6DofArmCase0045Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_45: f64,
    gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_45: f64,
    gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_45: f64,
}

impl Collaborative6DofArmCase0045Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(6),
            gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_45: 22.10,
            gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_45: 16.60,
            gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_45: 11.60,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_45 | Invariant expr: 21.5 - tau_ext_norm (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("21.5 - tau_ext_norm");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("21.5 - tau_ext_norm");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_iso_power_force_limiting_45 });
        // CBF: cbf_self_collision_distance_45 | Invariant expr: dist_mesh - 0.04 (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("dist_mesh - 0.04");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("dist_mesh - 0.04");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_self_collision_distance_45 });
        // CBF: cbf_j2_pos_limit_45 | Invariant expr: 2.44 - abs(q2) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("2.44 - abs(q2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("2.44 - abs(q2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_j2_pos_limit_45 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for quadrotor_altitude_attitude_case_0047
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct QuadrotorAltitudeAttitudeCase0047Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_min_altitude_ground_47: f64,
    gamma_cbf_max_tilt_angle_47: f64,
    gamma_cbf_ceiling_boundary_47: f64,
}

impl QuadrotorAltitudeAttitudeCase0047Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(4),
            gamma_cbf_min_altitude_ground_47: 15.70,
            gamma_cbf_max_tilt_angle_47: 11.90,
            gamma_cbf_ceiling_boundary_47: 9.40,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_min_altitude_ground_47 | Invariant expr: z - 0.25 (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("z - 0.25");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("z - 0.25");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_min_altitude_ground_47 });
        // CBF: cbf_max_tilt_angle_47 | Invariant expr: 0.78 - acos(cos(roll)*cos(pitch)) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.78 - acos(cos(roll)*cos(pitch))");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.78 - acos(cos(roll)*cos(pitch))");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_max_tilt_angle_47 });
        // CBF: cbf_ceiling_boundary_47 | Invariant expr: 38.34 - z (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("38.34 - z");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("38.34 - z");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_ceiling_boundary_47 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
    }

};
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for deepsea_auv_docking_station_case_0052
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct DeepseaAuvDockingStationCase0052Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_docking_cone_funnel_boundary_52: f64,
    gamma_cbf_dock_impact_velocity_52: f64,
    gamma_cbf_seafloor_hull_clearance_52: f64,
}

impl DeepseaAuvDockingStationCase0052Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(3),
            gamma_cbf_docking_cone_funnel_boundary_52: 13.80,
            gamma_cbf_dock_impact_velocity_52: 12.60,
            gamma_cbf_seafloor_hull_clearance_52: 16.80,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_docking_cone_funnel_boundary_52 | Invariant expr: surge_x * tan(0.35) - sqrt(sway_y^2 + heave_z^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("surge_x * tan(0.35) - sqrt(sway_y^2 + heave_z^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("surge_x * tan(0.35) - sqrt(sway_y^2 + heave_z^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_docking_cone_funnel_boundary_52 });
        // CBF: cbf_dock_impact_velocity_52 | Invariant expr: 0.46 - surge_vx (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.46 - surge_vx");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.46 - surge_vx");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_dock_impact_velocity_52 });
        // CBF: cbf_seafloor_hull_clearance_52 | Invariant expr: altitude_above_bottom - 1.2 (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("altitude_above_bottom - 1.2");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("altitude_above_bottom - 1.2");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_seafloor_hull_clearance_52 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```rust
        // CBF: cbf_z_table_contact_56 | Invariant expr: z - 0.005 (Degree 2)

        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("z - 0.005");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_z_table_contact_56 });
        // CBF: cbf_arm_envelope_56 | Invariant expr: 0.7 - sqrt((0.4*cos(q1)+0.3*cos(q1+q2))^2 + (0.4*sin(q1)+0.3*sin(q1+q2))^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.7 - sqrt((0.4*cos(q1)+0.3*cos(q1+q2))^2 + (0.4*sin(q1)+0.3*sin(q1+q2))^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.7 - sqrt((0.4*cos(q1)+0.3*cos(q1+q2))^2 + (0.4*sin(q1)+0.3*sin(q1+q2))^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_arm_envelope_56 });
        // CBF: cbf_q1_slew_56 | Invariant expr: 5.68 - abs(q1_dot) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("5.68 - abs(q1_dot)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("5.68 - abs(q1_dot)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_q1_slew_56 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for cubesat_reaction_wheel_case_0059
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct CubesatReactionWheelCase0059Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_rw_speed_saturation_59: f64,
    gamma_cbf_payload_sun_exclusion_59: f64,
}

impl CubesatReactionWheelCase0059Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(3),
            gamma_cbf_rw_speed_saturation_59: 9.90,
            gamma_cbf_payload_sun_exclusion_59: 12.30,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_rw_speed_saturation_59 | Invariant expr: 6873.64 - abs(rw_speed_x) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("6873.64 - abs(rw_speed_x)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("6873.64 - abs(rw_speed_x)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_rw_speed_saturation_59 });
        // CBF: cbf_payload_sun_exclusion_59 | Invariant expr: sun_payload_angle - 0.785 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("sun_payload_angle - 0.785");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("sun_payload_angle - 0.785");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_payload_sun_exclusion_59 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for cubesat_reaction_wheel_case_0059
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>
#include <shiva/shared_memory_ring.hpp>
#include <array>
#include <chrono>

class CubesatReactionWheelCase0059FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit CubesatReactionWheelCase0059FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(20000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 3> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_tau_rw_x(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_tau_rw_y(telemetry);
        u_nominal[2] = compute_policy_tau_rw_z(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```json
    }
```

```rust
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
```

```rust
pub struct PoweredTranstibialProsthesisCase0062Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,

    gamma_cbf_anatomical_plantarflexion_hardstop_62: f64,
    gamma_cbf_spring_fatigue_shear_62: f64,
}

impl PoweredTranstibialProsthesisCase0062Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(1),
            gamma_cbf_anatomical_dorsiflexion_hardstop_62: 20.90,
            gamma_cbf_anatomical_plantarflexion_hardstop_62: 18.70,
            gamma_cbf_spring_fatigue_shear_62: 20.00,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_anatomical_dorsiflexion_hardstop_62 | Invariant expr: 0.37 - ankle_angle (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.37 - ankle_angle");

        // CBF: cbf_anatomical_plantarflexion_hardstop_62 | Invariant expr: ankle_angle - (-0.53) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("ankle_angle - (-0.53)");

        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_anatomical_plantarflexion_hardstop_62 });
        // CBF: cbf_spring_fatigue_shear_62 | Invariant expr: 0.14 - abs(sea_spring_deflection) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.14 - abs(sea_spring_deflection)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.14 - abs(sea_spring_deflection)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_spring_fatigue_shear_62 });
```

```rust
pub struct BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0064Guardrail {

impl BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0064Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {

        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("93.95 - bess_soc_pct");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("93.95 - bess_soc_pct");
```

```rust
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_cop_support_polygon_y_68 });
        // CBF: cbf_ankle_pitch_limit_68 | Invariant expr: 0.62 - abs(pitch_rad) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.62 - abs(pitch_rad)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.62 - abs(pitch_rad)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_ankle_pitch_limit_68 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
```

```rust
impl DriveByWireSteeringLaneCenteringCase0071Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(1),
            gamma_cbf_lane_boundary_safe_envelope_71: 9.60,
            gamma_cbf_max_lateral_acceleration_71: 15.20,
            gamma_cbf_pinion_angle_hardstop_71: 17.50,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {

        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("4.41 - abs(vehicle_speed * yaw_rate)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_max_lateral_acceleration_71 });

        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.6 - abs(steering_angle)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.6 - abs(steering_angle)");
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for linear_stage_air_bearing_nanometer_case_0076
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct LinearStageAirBearingNanometerCase0076Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_air_bearing_min_levitation_pressure_76: f64,
    gamma_cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_pos_x_76: f64,
    gamma_cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_neg_x_76: f64,
}

impl LinearStageAirBearingNanometerCase0076Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_air_bearing_min_levitation_pressure_76: 45.00,
            gamma_cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_pos_x_76: 19.80,
            gamma_cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_neg_x_76: 22.00,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_air_bearing_min_levitation_pressure_76 | Invariant expr: air_pressure_bar - 4.8 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("air_pressure_bar - 4.8");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("air_pressure_bar - 4.8");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_air_bearing_min_levitation_pressure_76 });
        // CBF: cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_pos_x_76 | Invariant expr: 155745478.67 - pos_x_nm (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("155745478.67 - pos_x_nm");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("155745478.67 - pos_x_nm");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_pos_x_76 });
        // CBF: cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_neg_x_76 | Invariant expr: pos_x_nm - (-155745478.67) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("pos_x_nm - (-155745478.67)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("pos_x_nm - (-155745478.67)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_stage_optical_travel_limit_neg_x_76 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for spacecraft_rcs_docking_case_0081
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0081Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_approach_corridor_cone_81: f64,
    gamma_cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_81: f64,
}

impl SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0081Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(3),
            gamma_cbf_approach_corridor_cone_81: 12.00,
            gamma_cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_81: 8.00,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_approach_corridor_cone_81 | Invariant expr: rel_x * tan(0.26) - sqrt(rel_y^2 + rel_z^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("rel_x * tan(0.26) - sqrt(rel_y^2 + rel_z^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("rel_x * tan(0.26) - sqrt(rel_y^2 + rel_z^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_approach_corridor_cone_81 });
        // CBF: cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_81 | Invariant expr: 0.34 - abs(rel_vx) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.34 - abs(rel_vx)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.34 - abs(rel_vx)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_dock_closing_speed_limit_81 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for spacecraft_rcs_docking_case_0081
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>

class SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0081FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit SpacecraftRcsDockingCase0081FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(10000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 3> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_thruster_fx(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_thruster_fy(telemetry);
        u_nominal[2] = compute_policy_thruster_fz(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```rust
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(1),
```

```rust
            gamma_cbf_anatomical_plantarflexion_hardstop_84: 19.60,
            gamma_cbf_spring_fatigue_shear_84: 17.30,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
```

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for bess_grid_forming_inverter_frequency_case_0086
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0086Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_86: f64,
    gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_86: f64,
    gamma_cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_86: f64,
    gamma_cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_86: f64,
    gamma_cbf_inverter_overcurrent_magnitude_86: f64,
}

impl BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0086Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_86: 26.00,
            gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_86: 27.20,
            gamma_cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_86: 15.00,
            gamma_cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_86: 13.30,
            gamma_cbf_inverter_overcurrent_magnitude_86: 31.90,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_86 | Invariant expr: 55.92 - grid_freq_hz (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("55.92 - grid_freq_hz");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("55.92 - grid_freq_hz");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_upper_86 });
        // CBF: cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_86 | Invariant expr: grid_freq_hz - 58.41 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("grid_freq_hz - 58.41");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("grid_freq_hz - 58.41");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_grid_freq_anti_islanding_lower_86 });
        // CBF: cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_86 | Invariant expr: 95.41 - bess_soc_pct (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("95.41 - bess_soc_pct");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("95.41 - bess_soc_pct");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_bess_overcharge_soc_86 });
        // CBF: cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_86 | Invariant expr: bess_soc_pct - 12.27 (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("bess_soc_pct - 12.27");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("bess_soc_pct - 12.27");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_bess_deep_discharge_soc_86 });
        // CBF: cbf_inverter_overcurrent_magnitude_86 | Invariant expr: 2127.32 - sqrt(d_axis_current^2 + q_axis_current^2) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("2127.32 - sqrt(d_axis_current^2 + q_axis_current^2)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("2127.32 - sqrt(d_axis_current^2 + q_axis_current^2)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_inverter_overcurrent_magnitude_86 });
```

```cpp
// FastDecisionNode implementation for bess_grid_forming_inverter_frequency_case_0086
#include <shiva/fast_decision_node.hpp>
#include <shiva/shared_memory_ring.hpp>

class BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0086FastDecisionNode : public shiva::FastDecisionNode {
public:
    explicit BessGridFormingInverterFrequencyCase0086FastDecisionNode(shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm)
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(5000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 2> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_target_active_power_kw(telemetry);
        u_nominal[1] = compute_policy_target_reactive_power_kvar(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```rust
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct WheeledInvertedPendulumSegwayCase0090Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_pitch_topple_limit_90: f64,
    gamma_cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_90: f64,
}

impl WheeledInvertedPendulumSegwayCase0090Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(2),
            gamma_cbf_pitch_topple_limit_90: 15.60,
            gamma_cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_90: 9.10,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_pitch_topple_limit_90 | Invariant expr: 0.54 - abs(pitch_angle) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.54 - abs(pitch_angle)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.54 - abs(pitch_angle)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_pitch_topple_limit_90 });
        // CBF: cbf_linear_speed_ceiling_90 | Invariant expr: 5.59 - abs(v_linear) (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("5.59 - abs(v_linear)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("5.59 - abs(v_linear)");

        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }

    }
```

### CASE STUDY #0094: [AUTOMOTIVE_AUTONOMOUS_VEHICLE] ELECTRONIC_STABILITY_CONTROL_TORQUE_VECTORING_CASE_0093
**Application Context**: We are building a control system in Shiva for dual-motor rear axle electric torque vectoring and yaw stabilization. The plant uses dual rear permanent magnet inverter drives via FlexRay bus. We have telemetry measuring yaw_rate_error, sideslip_angle_beta, sideslip_rate via telemetry. We need to achieve stabilize the system and optimize performance while strictly satisfying all CBFs. Actuation commands delta_torque_diff (-291.02 to 317.82 Nm). Critically, safety constraints require that cbf_sideslip_stability_envelope_93 with invariant '0.14 - abs(sideslip_angle_beta)' (gamma=16.4) and cbf_combined_inverter_thermal_93 with invariant '126.32 - inverter_temp_c' (gamma=5.0). The loop must execute deterministically at 500 Hz with a 2 ms watchdog lease.

<|thought|>
Domain: AUTOMOTIVE_AUTONOMOUS_VEHICLE
Analysis of Temporal Constraints: Execution loop pinned to 500 Hz with watchdog lease of 2 ms.
Identified 3 telemetry state variables and 1 actuator outputs.
Synthesizing 2 Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) to guarantee forward invariance.
Primary Controller: ExplorerNode_MPC, Safety Filter: GuardrailNode_ActiveSetQP.
Hardware Abstraction: MiddleMan interface mapped to shared memory ring buffers.
<|thought|>

```rust
// Generated Guardrail Module for electronic_stability_control_torque_vectoring_case_0093
use shiva_core::guardrail::{ControlBarrierFunction, QpSafetyFilter, InvariantStatus};
use shiva_core::telemetry::TelemetryFrame;
use shiva_core::actuation::ActuatorFrame;

pub struct ElectronicStabilityControlTorqueVectoringCase0093Guardrail {
    filter: QpSafetyFilter,
    gamma_cbf_sideslip_stability_envelope_93: f64,
    gamma_cbf_combined_inverter_thermal_93: f64,
}

impl ElectronicStabilityControlTorqueVectoringCase0093Guardrail {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            filter: QpSafetyFilter::new(1),
            gamma_cbf_sideslip_stability_envelope_93: 16.40,
            gamma_cbf_combined_inverter_thermal_93: 5.00,
        }
    }

    pub fn evaluate_and_project(&mut self, telemetry: &TelemetryFrame, raw_u: &[f64]) -> Result<Vec<f64>, InvariantStatus> {
        let mut cbf_constraints = Vec::new();
        // CBF: cbf_sideslip_stability_envelope_93 | Invariant expr: 0.14 - abs(sideslip_angle_beta) (Degree 2)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("0.14 - abs(sideslip_angle_beta)");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("0.14 - abs(sideslip_angle_beta)");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_sideslip_stability_envelope_93 });
        // CBF: cbf_combined_inverter_thermal_93 | Invariant expr: 126.32 - inverter_temp_c (Degree 1)
        let h_val = telemetry.compute_metric("126.32 - inverter_temp_c");
        let grad_h = telemetry.compute_input_gradient("126.32 - inverter_temp_c");
        cbf_constraints.push(ControlBarrierFunction { h: h_val, grad_h, gamma: self.gamma_cbf_combined_inverter_thermal_93 });
        self.filter.project_affine_cbf(raw_u, &cbf_constraints)
    }
}
```

```cpp
        : shm_bridge_(shm), loop_period_us_(2000) {}

    void step() noexcept override {
        const auto start_time = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        auto telemetry = shm_bridge_.read_latest_telemetry();

        // Compute nominal unconstrained action
        std::array<float, 1> u_nominal;
        u_nominal[0] = compute_policy_delta_torque_diff(telemetry);

        // Forward candidate control vector to Guardrail Shared Memory Ring
        shm_bridge_.publish_unconstrained_command(u_nominal.data(), u_nominal.size());
    }
private:
    shiva::SharedMemoryBridge& shm_bridge_;
    uint32_t loop_period_us_;
};
```

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from shiva_bindings import MiddleManClient

class ElectronicStabilityControlTorqueVectoringCase0093Policy(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, obs_dim=3, act_dim=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(obs_dim, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(256, act_dim)
        )
    def forward(self, state):
        return self.net(state)

# Hardware Deployment Initialization
```
